title: Selling the Shetland pony to buy an instrument
summary: His father would not buy him a keyboard instrument, so he sold his pony for $100; he tells how he got the pony and other boyhood doings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When I went from Rolla, back home I kept yearning for that. So I asked my dad to get one. And he wouldn't he said no. I think he was disappointed in my brother's stopping the violin.
Yeah.
And I don't think he thought I had anything
-- I didn't show too much, I think, in his mind that would warrant him going out and spending the money. So I had a pony --
yeah.
So I sold the pony, I got a $100.00. It was a Shetland, nice Shetland pony and I sold it and --
How did you have the pony -- when did you get the pony?
Well, we had it -- it was my older brothers, and then when he went to college he said, he came back one summer and I was taking care of it and he'd gone to college and --
Yeah.

So he said to me, I think you're big enough, he said, he was hitched out in front of the house. He said, I'm going to start in about 10 seconds and if you can ride him around -- tell me where to ride him, if you can ride him in so-and-so time, he's yours. And my mother was in the back and she looked up and here I had him wide open and she said, he's running with Ken, he's running away with Ken. She came running out in the front front lawn. And I pulled up in front of the house and he said, "No, I just told him he had to make it in so many seconds." So many minutes or something. And, so I made it so he said, I'm giving him the pony, so that's how I happened to have it. But I --

Well I -- I never had a bicycle, I rode -- all I did was ride the pony -- I'd ride into town for groceries and get on, both arms and just ride --
Saddled? He was saddled?
Ah --
The pony had a saddle on?
Oh, yeah, I had a surrey too.
Oh, really?
Yeah had a two-cart surrey --
How about that?
-- I used to -- oh on Saturdays I'd go out to -- oh little town like Frederick and collect walnuts and things like that --
Yeah, yeah. And earn a little money, you mean, with it?
What?
Earn a little money with them, would you sell them?
I'd keep them myself.
OH, that was nice.
Walnuts -- black walnuts are beautiful.
Yeah.
In the wintertime, you know, in fudge, it's good --
Yeah.
-- cold weather -- course we had no radio or anything like that in those days.
No, that's right. Yeah. Had to make your own fun.
Read -- yeah there was no radio or television.
